Hopkins, of Lancashire W.C., led, followed by our Fred Bentley. Colin Sutton was fourth, and we had several men between tenth and twentieth positions.

The great feature of the race was the tussle which developed between the Olympic champion and our Fred Bentley. With the possibility of International selection for the European Games next September to spur them on, both men gave of their best.
Fred Bentley was, of course, in France representing Great Britain at the European Games. Jack Bidgood found the pressure of work in a new position prevented him from training.
We hope to see him a Club Vice-President in years to come. How does Fred Bentley find life in the R.A.F.? What does Harry Shields think of war-time rationing?
Fred Bentley, our well-known police long distance walker, having gained his wings in Canada, came home to meet with an accident which has partially paralysed his left shoulder.
Fred Bentley has been invalided out of the Police after his accident in a plane. He has now started business at the Post Office, Blackmore, Liss, Hants.

From 1924 to 1939, a period of 16 years, the race was won eight times by Fred Rickards and four times by Fred Bentley. Now, after trying for 21 years, our vice-captain, Jack Bidgood, has added his name to the list of Belgrave successes, beating Tom Kent, the winner for the past three years, over the last mile.
Much could be written of Tommy Green’s magnificent performances and those of Fred Rickards, Fred Bentley and others, but space does not permit.

Fred Rickards, Fred Bentley and Hugh have all won on three successive occasions and Hugh looked all set for it this year. However that very improved young walker, McFarlane of the Poly, who incidentally seems to spend more time with us than his own club, beat Mc.to it and so the battle for this honour still goes on.

Names like Fred Rickards, Fred Bentley, and Jack Bidgood remind us of the past years, but now it would seem that George Checkley and Hugh McGreechan have taken on the task of keeping a Belgrave name on the trophy.

It goes without saying that Tommy as a member of the winning Belgrave team was always in the awards, and together with his close companions of those days Fred Rickard and Fred Bentley, provided an unbeatable trio.

Others deserving our congratulations are Fred Bentley, who was placed second in both 20 Miles and 50 Kilos events; and Joe Coleman and Len Coleman, who dead-heated in the "Junior" Championship for first place.

The Chief Judge at the Chippenham to Calne Walk was George Bentley now living at Portishead, Avon. He looked fit and well and told us that his brother Fred, one of our great long-distance walkers of the 30's and an international in 1938, was also fit and well.

One of a good number of Metropolitan Policemen who have served Belgrave well - brother of the renowned Fred Bentley he walked in many of our club teams and in 1947 he finished 5th in National Junior 10 Miles in which Belgrave finished 2nd team.
Our leading 50k walker was Fred Bentley and the RWA Championship was held, on Whit Monday at Bradford, where the local race was of long standing (1903).
